/usr/lib/apt/methods/http.why: Browsers can't open TCP connections: Shiro's transport fetches from the page's same-origin mirror. apt still verifies the signed InRelease and every hash.

/usr/lib/apt/methods/store.why: apt decompresses every downloaded index through this method; under the x86 engine xz-decoding trixie's 56 MB Packages took ~33 s of `apt-get update`. Shiro's runs the same codecs and hashes natively; apt still checks the result against the signed Release file.

/usr/sbin/dpkg-preconfigure.why: apt-utils' 70debconf hook runs this before every dpkg run; under DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive it has nothing to ask but cost ~20 s per install under the x86 engine (Perl, debconf, apt-extracttemplates). Shiro's drains apt's list and exits 0 then (templates load at configure time through the confmodule, as without apt-utils) and runs Debian's script, kept as dpkg-preconfigure.debian, for any other frontend.
